title: Project skills and plugin controls — contract

steps.path: Projects → a project → Skills & tools, the skill drawer, and Marketplace install
steps.headline: This is what done means for project skills and plugin controls, before Your Assistant's locked switches arrive.

rows.statement: An automatically enabled skill lets the assistant know it exists, and it reads that skill's full instructions only when it's actually used.
A skill you add yourself outside the marketplace keeps behaving the way it does today, with no extra step required to enable it.
Turning on a plugin's server or hook automatically shows a risk warning; an automatically discoverable skill alone does not trigger that warning.
An existing project's switches first show which skills and tools already work there today, rather than starting from a blank default.
A personal skill missing on this device shows the saved choice and explains it needs to be added here; syncing the file is later work.
An item installed from outside the marketplace and missing here stays visible with an explanation that it needs local setup, instead of disappearing.
These project switches control only YouCoded's own assistant for now; Claude Code's settings are left untouched.
Each project and its plugin use the app's own collapsible-card style, with each skill and the server as its own card inside, evenly padded.
At phone width, all four project tabs stay reachable; the open tab shows its name while the others keep their icons.
Managing which skills and tools are automatic lives inside the Projects screen you already use, alongside its other tabs, not a separate page.
The Skills & tools tab fills the same width as the project's Files and Instructions & Memories tabs, with matching group headings and full-width rows.
On a phone, a plugin shows as one full-width row with its skills and server inset below; a missing item uses the same shape.
On a narrow phone screen, each skill's automatic, manual or unavailable status stays readable beside its plugin badge.
Clicking an unavailable skill's card closes the drawer and opens Projects on Skills & tools, scrolled to that missing item's row.
An already-open conversation keeps showing the skill availability it started with; a note explains that a changed switch applies to your next new conversation.
'Set up here' offers to ask the assistant to fix a missing item, or choose the file yourself for a missing personal skill.
On Android, the Skills & tools tab stays visible and editable, with a note that its switches don't affect phone conversations yet.
Each skill's status chip sits at the card's right edge, colored like the session switcher; clicking the chip or its dimmed card opens its setup.
After you install a plugin, the same window lists your projects so you can turn it on only where you want; it starts off everywhere.
On a phone, the marketplace install panel opens with the first project already expanded, so its plugin and skill show without an extra tap.
On a phone, a setup row's description wraps onto a second line instead of cutting off, and both buttons say Set up here.
Pressing 'Set up here' for something missing on this device opens a popup explaining why, instead of expanding inside the card.
Switching on a plugin that can reach outside services shows a popup first, naming those connections, before it actually turns on.
